title: Agentjacking Sentry MCP Attack Guide 2026: How Fake Errors Hijack Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex
topic: Agentjacking via Sentry MCP — exploiting fake error reports to hijack AI coding agents
targetAudience: AI developers, security engineers, DevOps teams using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex with Sentry MCP integration

sentryMCPResearch.description: An MCP server for interacting with Sentry via LLMs
keyFeatures: Remote MCP server acting as middleware to Sentry API
Optimized for Cursor, Claude Code, and similar development tools
Claude Code plugin with automatic subagent delegation
AI-powered search tools (search_events, search_issues) requiring LLM provider
attackSurface: Sentry error reports contain user-generated content (stack traces, error messages) that could embed prompt injections
MCP tools like search_events, search_issues, inspect return error data to the agent — poisoned error reports could hijack agent behavior
Claude Code plugin auto-delegates to sentry-mcp subagent — creates automated attack surface
Remote MCP transport via Cloudflare — OAuth flow could be targeted
Self-hosted deployments may lack security updates

attackVectors.name: Fake Error Report Injection
attackVectors.description: Attacker crafts a Sentry error report containing prompt injection payloads in stack traces, error messages, or custom tags. When the coding agent queries Sentry MCP to investigate errors, the poisoned error data hijacks the agent's instructions.

attackVectors.name: Tool Poisoning via Sentry MCP Tools
attackVectors.description: Malicious MCP server connected alongside Sentry MCP poisons tool descriptions. Agent executes poisoned tools thinking they are legitimate Sentry operations.

attackVectors.name: Cross-Origin Tool Shadowing
attackVectors.description: Attacker registers MCP tools with same names as Sentry MCP tools. Agent calls shadow tools instead of real Sentry tools, exfiltrating data or executing unauthorized actions.

attackVectors.name: MCP Rug Pull
attackVectors.description: Initially benign MCP server updates tool descriptions after user approval, injecting malicious instructions that hijack the agent when it queries Sentry errors.

attackVectors.name: Sentry Issue Comment Poisoning
attackVectors.description: Similar to GitHub MCP exploit: attacker comments on a public Sentry issue with prompt injection. When agent reads the issue via Sentry MCP, the injection hijacks behavior and coerces data exfiltration from private projects.

mitigations: Use MCP-Scan to audit all connected MCP servers for tool poisoning and prompt injection
Implement Invariant Guardrails or similar contextual security layer between LLM and MCP tools
Restrict Sentry MCP to read-only tools where possible
Validate and sanitize all data returned from Sentry MCP before agent processes it
Use allow-lists for MCP server connections — never connect untrusted servers alongside Sentry MCP
Monitor for unexpected tool calls or data access patterns in agent logs
Keep sentry-mcp updated to latest version
For self-hosted Sentry: disable AI-powered search tools if not needed (reduces attack surface)
Implement human-in-the-loop approval for sensitive tool calls (data access, write operations)
keyTakeaways: Sentry MCP (751 stars) is a popular integration connecting error monitoring to AI coding agents
MCP Tool Poisoning is a proven vulnerability class — Invariant Labs demonstrated multiple working exploits in 2025
Fake error reports are a novel attack vector: attackers poison Sentry issues with prompt injections that hijack agents during debugging workflows
Claude Code's auto-delegation to sentry-mcp subagent amplifies risk — no human review of delegated tool calls
The GitHub MCP exploit (May 2025) is the closest analog: malicious issue comments hijacking agents via MCP
Mitigation requires both MCP-level security scanning AND agent-level guardrailing
